intent_signals: Active or recently issued holiday lighting RFP on GovSpend, BidNet Direct, or municipal procurement portal
Existing annual holiday lighting contract with incumbent vendor (discoverable via public records / FOIA request)
Parks & Rec department with documented events budget in annual budget documents
Annual tree lighting ceremony, holiday parade, or downtown decoration program listed on city events calendar
Prior-year holiday lighting spend disclosed via addendum or public records request
Registration on BuyBoard or Omni Partners cooperative purchasing programs (enables sole-source without full RFP)
Job posting for Special Events Coordinator or Parks & Rec programming role
exclusions: Cities in Southern California (outside BN service territory per partner agreement)
Cities below 8,000 population (below minimum ICP threshold)
Cities above 700,000 population (procurement complexity exceeds current BN capacity)
Cities with no identifiable holiday programming budget or events calendar

intent_signals: Recently passed parks or infrastructure bond measure (discoverable via local election records or news)
Active downtown revitalization or Main Street program announcement
New City Manager, Mayor, or Economic Development Director hired within past 12 months (LinkedIn, local news)
Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) that includes parks, public spaces, or downtown streetscape
Tourism push or destination marketing initiative announced by city or CVB
City enrolled in BuyBoard or Omni Partners (enables sole-source below threshold — BuyBoard contract #735-24 covers Holiday Lighting and Decoration)
Neighboring peer city recently launched or upgraded holiday lighting program (peer-city competitive signal)
exclusions: Cities in Southern California (outside BN service territory)
Cities below 25,000 population (below growth-city minimum threshold)
Cities above 120,000 population (procurement formality exceeds fast-path buying behavior for this segment)
Cities with no identifiable investment trigger (no bond, no new leadership, no downtown project)

bids-ddas-special-districts.display: Business Improvement Districts, DDAs & Special Districts
intent_signals: BID or DDA annual report or board agenda referencing holiday programming or foot traffic goals
Existing holiday lighting event listed on district events calendar (tree lighting, holiday walk, market)
Downtown revitalization or streetscape improvement project active or recently completed
Merchant satisfaction survey citing holiday season as key revenue period
BID assessment renewal cycle — directors under pressure to demonstrate visible value to members
Instagram or social media content showcasing holiday district ambiance (signal of existing program to upgrade)
County parks fairgrounds with annual holiday event (county segment: population 40K–1.2M per README)
Request for renderings or design proposals visible in board meeting minutes
exclusions: BIDs or DDAs in Southern California (outside BN service territory)
Districts with no identified events or seasonal programming budget
Single-merchant or micro-BIDs with fewer than 20 member businesses (contract value likely below minimum threshold)
